stories.title: Patriots place RB TreVeyon Henderson on IR with still unexplained illness
stories.summary: The Patriots placed RB TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve while he deals with an unexplained neurological issue.
stories.detail: MUNICH -- The New England Patriots placed running back TreVeyon Henderson on injured reserve Saturday, eight days after Henderson said he recently experienced "an unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms." Henderson had already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions at FC Bayern Munich Arena (9:30 a.m. ET, Fox) earlier in the week. He now will miss at least the next four games. Henderson has said that tests have "come back positive and reassuring," and in a social media post said, "the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable." The Patriots entered the week with just two healthy running backs -- Corey Kiner and Lan Larison -- as starter Rhamondre Stevenson was managing a knee tendon injury sustained in last Sunday's loss to the Green Bay Packers . Stevenson was a limited participant in the Patriots' two practices in Munich, and coach Mike Vrabel said Friday he was feeling "pretty good" when asked to gauge Stevenson's potential availability for the game at that point. Vrabel said the same thing about wide receiver A.J. Brown , who has missed the past two games with a knee flare-up. A potential tipoff…

stories.title: What placing TreVeyon Henderson on IR, activating Greg Van Roten and Reggie Gilliam means for the Patriots
stories.summary: The Patriots made three roster moves ahead of their game against the Lions.
stories.detail: At around 10 p.m. local time in Germany on Saturday, the New England Patriots announced that they have made some changes to their roster . Running back TreVeyon Henderson was headed to injured reserve due to the illness that has kept him out since late October, while fullback Reggie Gilliam and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten were both activated from IR. With the Patriots having entered the weekend at 52 players on their roster, Saturday’s transactions meant that they now have a full complement of players available again. What else do the moves mean, though? Let’s find out. RB TreVeyon Henderson: Placed on IR TreVeyon Henderson taking to social media last Friday already was an ominous sign. In a statement addressing the illness that had kept him out for more than a week at that point, he mentioned that “my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions” were affected by the “unexpected and unusual medical emergency” he had been dealing with. While there might still have been hope at that point that he would be able to return in a relatively short period of time, Saturday’s move means that that will not be the case. Henderson will be out for at least the next four games…

London does lower his head as he makes contact with the Bengals defender on his way out of bounds, but does this really rise to the level of a $24k fine? (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are about to enter a new era of their franchise. Fernando Mendoza will make his first start and hopes to make an impact on the field. They’ll face one of the toughest defenses in football. Of course, after five of their last six games, any spark will help this team take the next step. The excitement from the fanbase about seeing their young quarterback should help fill the seats for a key home game. However, the losses have eroded confidence in the team’s direction over the past few weeks. While before it hit 99% on Week 3 it is now down to 78% heading into Week 10. Hopefully, Mendoza’s play can boost the fan base’s confidence. The team’s young talent is playing well, with Brock Bowers and Treydan Stukes making plays every week. stories.detail: Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves will not play against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday because of a left heel bruise, the team announced. Lakers coach JJ Redick had previously said Reaves would be "day-to-day" while dealing with the injury, which he suffered in Wednesday's 123-112 road win over the Milwaukee Bucks while landing awkwardly after missing a contested fastbreak dunk attempt. When the doors opened for Lakers practice Saturday and reporters were let in, Reaves could be seen on the sidelines wearing slide sandals -- but without any wrap or boot on his left foot. Redick said that Reaves did not practice, staying off his feet to help the bruise heal. stories.title: 76ers' Joel Embiid out vs. Pacers due to plantar fascia management
stories.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers ruled out center Joel Embiid for Sunday's game against the Indiana Pacers with right foot plantar fascia management, the team announced Saturday.
stories.detail: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers ruled out center Joel Embiid for Sunday's game against the Indiana Pacers with right foot plantar fascia management, the team announced Saturday. Big men Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Dominick Barlow (back) are also out. Barlow hasn't played this season, and coach Nick Nurse said Saturday that he is "progressing" but has no timeline for his return. LeBron James , who missed Thursday's win over the Toronto Raptors with sciatica and low back management, wasn't listed on the injury report. Without Embiid, Bona and Barlow, the Sixers will be significantly thin in the frontcourt. Tacko Fall , a two-way player, is the only active center on the roster. The Sixers will likely lean on James, Jabari Walker and Dean Wade to fill in the responsibilities at center. The Sixers are 1-1 without Embiid this season. In those games, James started the first at center -- a loss to Detroit -- and then Bona in a win against the Hornets. stories.detail: Lakers coach JJ Redick slaps hand with forward Ziaire Williams as he comes off the court during a timeout. (Gina Ferazzi/Los Angeles Times) While rocketing toward the top of the league, the Lakers have been far from perfect. That’s good news to them. “A big thing that we talk with our players about a lot is being able to learn and get better and try to correct things even when you are winning,” coach JJ Redick said. The Lakers (11-2) have won seven consecutive games entering Sunday’s 1 p.m. PST matinee against the Suns (5-6) in Phoenix. Using a rare multiple-day break between games to audit their performances, coaches and analytics staffers showed slide presentations to players about both offensive and defensive flaws this week. The lectures left the team with one of the best records in the league feeling as if it was one of the worst, forward Ziaire Williams joked. Already the top-ranked offense in the league, the Lakers should strive to match that by becoming a top-10 defense, Redick implored his team. teamStories.detail: SAN ANTONIO -- In his first game as the primary offensive engine in place of the injured Stephen Curry , Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg went 1-of-13 shooting in a 123-85 blowout loss to the San Antonio Spurs on Friday night. "We just lost by like 100," Lendeborg said. "So you know I'm f---ed up mentally right now." Twelve hours earlier, following the team's morning shootaround in San Antonio, Lendeborg expressed an apprehensive excitement about his elevated scoring role in place of Curry, placing his confidence level at a "6 out of 10." "The other four is like, man, am I going to be able to live up to it?" Lendeborg said. "Am I going to be able to help out the team the way I want to? But time will tell." Lendeborg has had a generally spectacular start to his NBA career, averaging 21.7 points and 7.4 rebounds through his first 12 games and generating early Rookie of the Year buzz. He had 37 points in a win over the LA Clippers when Curry rested earlier in the month. But the Clippers aren't the Spurs.
